subject: Urgent: capacity tiebreak rule exception for HelioVent Q4 launch
messages:
From: Sara Park <sara.park@heliovent.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@heliovent.com
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Urgent: capacity tiebreak rule exception for HelioVent Q4 launch

Jonas / Laura,

Quick heads-up — HelioVent has accelerated their user-facing rollout and we now expect a 3x spike in inference traffic starting the week of Oct 28. The attached forecast and the updated SOW (HLV-3321_SOW_v3.pdf) show a sustained increase for ~6 weeks tied to a partner promotion.

Our engineering and product teams ran a local opt test; to hit the latency targets they need the equivalent of an additional 8 A100-class GPUs reserved for a 6-week window (2026-10-28 to 2026-12-09) with minimal preemption.

We understand Redwood has a tiebreak/priority framework for dedicated capacity. Given HelioVent's renewal cadence and planned expansion, we are formally requesting an exception to the standard slice rules and asking for an answer by Oct 15 so we can finalize our launch plans.

Attachments: heliovent_traffic_forecast_Q4.xlsx, HLV-3321_SOW_v3.pdf

Can you confirm feasibility and any gating terms?

Thanks — Sara

Subject: Re: Urgent: capacity tiebreak rule exception for HelioVent Q4 launch

Sara — thanks for the data and the clear ask. I'm pulling operations and sales into this thread to assess options. Short answers up front: we want to avoid surprise preemption during your launch window, but we also have multiple committed deals in the same timeframe.

Laura / Markus / Ben — tag you for visibility. Per INF-7210 our default is to allocate by committed tranche + ARR-weighted tiebreaks; exceptions are possible but require an operational mitigation plan and an amendment to terms.

Markus — can ops give an initial feasibility read (current utilization, shard availability) and two options we can put on the table?

Ben — is HelioVent in the renewal/expansion cohort we should prioritize (I know there's a close date late Q4)?

Sara — we'll do our best to get you a concrete proposal by EOD Oct 14. If we need legal / procurement signoff we'll flag it.

— Jonas

On Mon, Oct 12, 2026 at 10:03 AM Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com> wrote:
> Markus — can ops give an initial feasibility read (current utilization, shard availability) and two options we can put on the table?

Quick feasibility notes (ops):
- Region pool (us-west-2, dedicated) current steady utilization: 92% across reserved tranches for Oct 25 — Nov 15.
- We have limited spare contiguous shards that can provide non-preemptible residency; most spare capacity is in preemptible burst pools.
- Impact of granting 8 A100-eq reserve: would require either migrating two smaller reserved deals to another tranche or reassigning 6 burst GPUs for the window. That triggers SLA implications for the other customers.

Two practical options to propose to HelioVent:
1) Partial guaranteed tranche: reserve 6 A100-eq GPUs for 5 weeks (2026-10-28 to 2026-11-30) as a dedicated, low-preempt slot + 2 A100-eq as burst capacity. This minimizes displacement risk and keeps SLAs for others with minor adjustments.

2) Virtualized scale + model-level concessions: keep current dedicated commit but give HelioVent a higher-concurrency route to a quantized model variant (4-bit weights) that reduces GPU requirements by ~40% for their workload, plus a reserved 2-GPU canary during peak hours. This preserves existing commits but accepts a potential quality delta.

Both options require:
- Amendment signed by Oct 16 (to lock scheduling and billing).
- A canary week (Oct 28–Nov 3) with detailed telemetry hooks enabled (token-level latency traces).
- Ops-run KV/prefix cache priming plan to reduce cold-start token costs.

I'll attach an ops cost delta sheet and a shard map but attaching as a stub here: ops_capacity_delta_calc_Q4.xlsx.

— Markus
Head of Platform Operations, Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Urgent: capacity tiebreak rule exception for HelioVent Q4 launch

Folks — adding commercial context: HelioVent is on track to renew in mid-November and their expansion (if we support this launch cleanly) materially increases our usage footprint and upsell motions. Current forecast (HubSpot HLV-3321) shows ~ $2.8M ARR potential with the next 12 months of committed usage.

Commercially I recommend we make a trade: grant option (1) from Ops (partial guaranteed tranche) but only if HelioVent executes a 12-month amendment extending their committed minimum and pays a 20% uplift for the guaranteed tranche. This preserves economics for displaced customers and locks HelioVent into a longer term.

If marketing value / references matter, we can add a joint case study clause as an incentive.

— Ben
Director, Sales — Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Date: Fri, 15 Oct 2026 17:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Urgent: capacity tiebreak rule exception for HelioVent Q4 launch

Sara — next steps and final decision: thank you for the fast turnaround on the forecast. After weighing operational constraints and commercial impact we will approve a conditional tranche as follows:

- Commitment: reserve 6 A100-equivalent GPUs (non-preemptible) for 5 weeks (2026-10-28 to 2026-11-30).
- Burst: additional 2 A100-equivalent GPUs available as preemptible burst during the same window.
- Commercial terms: HelioVent signs a 12-month amendment to HLV-3321 with a 20% uplift on the reserved tranche by Oct 16. DocuSign link: https://redwood.sign/HLV-3321-amendment (placeholder).
- Canary: we require the canary week (Oct 28–Nov 3) with telemetry hooks enabled and a joint runbook to validate latency and KV cache priming.
- Ops action: Markus to allocate shards and prepare autoscale policies + pre-warming scripts; Laura to approve the scheduling migration plan for any displaced tranches.

If HelioVent can sign the amendment by Oct 16 we will schedule the reserve and certify readiness for Oct 28. If not signed, we can offer option (2) (quantized model route + smaller reserved canary) as a fallback.

Forwarded for visibility: INF-7210 ticket and the ops capacity calc have been linked to the HubSpot deal.

— Jonas
VP, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
